store: Treasure Hoard round 1: an open Viking-age coffer on two hewn runners, low front; Amber tray (left), coin well (middle), Ruby tray (right front), Amber Pearl tray (right back); one kind per compartment, heaped and crowned over the rim when full

frame.atlas_sources: rows 0-31 hewn timber, 32-63 x0-63 end grain, 64-79 dark iron: assets/bunker_r4; 32-63 x64-95 dark oiled timber, x96-127 wear swatch: assets/metalpallet_r3; 80-111: fur hide, spotted fur hide, madder wool cloth, leather (new)

space: Unity prefab space, origin = footprint centre on the ground. Blender z-up/-y front -> Unity y-up/+z front: ux=-bx, uy=bz, uz=-by. OBJ export (forward NEGATIVE_Z, up Y) writes (bx, bz, -by); Unity's importer negates x, same mapping.
unit_semantics: SETTLED: every copy has an explicit final pose from a rigid-body simulation (convex-hull items, friction 0.75, restitution 0), dropped in batches onto the frozen earlier copies; each compartment's copy sequence is cut into its units in drop order. Each copy: the item's bounds centre at unit.position + copy.offset (= copy.world_position), rotated by copy.quat_xyzw (or copy.euler, Unity ZXY), longest side fit_longest_m. unit.position = centre of unit.box = the bounding box of the unit's copies, its bottom lowered to the lowest rotated-bounds corner (the never-below-the-floor lift leaves every settled copy alone).
fill_order: units are listed in fill order (interleaved over the compartments); within a compartment its units fill bottom up. Show the first n copies of a unit for a partial stack. Later copies rest on earlier ones, earlier ones never move. One item kind per compartment (compartment 0 Amber, 1 Coins, 2 Ruby, 3 Amber Pearl).

AmberPearl.note: The prefab's model is attach/model: a MeshRenderer with Unity's built-in Sphere (default resources mesh 10207) at scale 0.15 (0.15 m), 0.088 m up, plus a ParticleSystem glow. The rip cannot read built-in meshes, so this tray was laid out with a UV-sphere stand-in of that size; the mod draws the game's own sphere and material (ItemVisual takes MeshRenderers and skips the ParticleSystemRenderer).
